title: improv·artist · topographic (Tara Donovan)
mutation_directive: improv artist: topographic via Tara Donovan

improv_extras.practice: millions of identical objects (cups, pins, buttons) into landscape

v1.feedback: The topographic contour concept lands well — stacked differential-growth rings rendered as identical pins clearly channels Donovan's accumulation logic, and the warm-white-on-dark palette is restrained. The pin height encoding (taller at peak, shorter at base) is a smart readability choice, but 6K instanced cylinders at r=0.035 reads visually sparse for a Donovan piece that should feel like overwhelming material density; push MAX_PINS to 20K+ and shrink PIN_RADIUS to 0.015 so the surface feels packed rather than dotted. The slow orbital camera is fine but the breathing oscillation on contour heights is barely perceptible — either amplify it so the landscape visibly inhales or remove it to save the compute. Consider sampling pins along the filled interior of each contour ring (not just the perimeter) so the terrain reads as a solid topographic surface rather than concentric wire loops with pins on them.

v2.feedback: The idea lands well — differential growth rings rasterised into a heightfield of identical pins is a faithful Tara Donovan translation, and the topographic contour layering is legible within 2 seconds. The bone-white-on-near-black palette is restrained and appropriate. Two things to push: the breathing animation is subtle enough to feel like a screensaver wobble rather than earned motion — consider a slower, more localised wave (e.g. radial ripple from center outward) so the topography itself appears to shift like a living survey map. Second, the camera starts far enough that the individual pin identity is lost at default zoom; tighten the FOV or pull the camera closer so viewers immediately read 'thousands of identical cylinders' rather than a smooth surface, since that material-unit legibility is the core of Donovan's practice.
